Subject: SDK grace-period + rate-limit spike during ingest

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Quick heads-up — during our morning ingest window (around 08:55–09:05 PT) we saw a sharp series of 429s coming back from Redwood even though our overall QPS was within the contract cap. We were using the official JS SDK (v2.6.1) and observed the client retry/backoff behavior aligning into a crowd — the server-side 429s appear to be transient, then a short drop in throughput, then a big retry wave.

I attached a short extract of api logs and a timeline in the attachment. This is blocking our rollout to a second region — if we don’t get predictable behavior we’ll need to throttle more aggressively and that costs us margin.

Can someone on your side advise whether this is expected with the grace-period behavior we discussed last quarter? We need either an immediate mitigation or a clear mitigation-plan (short timeline).

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: SDK grace-period + rate-limit spike during ingest — repro notes

I dug into Ben’s logs and ran a local repro using the same JS SDK version (v2.6.1) against a staging replica. Observations: 
- When a mid-sized batch of clients hit a short upstream degradation, the SDKs backoff windows drift to align (no jitter) and then retry in waves.
- Redwood’s current "grace window" behavior in the routing layer temporarily allows additional in-flight for routes recently at capacity to avoid immediate 503s; that plus aligned retries creates short overload bursts and hard 429s once the burst finishes.

Repro script (summary): spawn 200 simulated connections with identical backoff parameters -> throttle server for 3s -> observe burst of retries and 429s. I can drop the repro into a repo if useful.

Short-term mitigation suggestions (field):
1) Client: add jitter/randomization to SDK backoff defaults and reduce maxInflight default to 8 (we currently default to 16 for throughput).
2) Server: reduce grace-window for the affected customer namespace to 500ms instead of 5s; this prevents the smoothing effect causing the spike.

I’ve attached a short extract of the API logs Ben provided for clarity.

Will file an RFC for the SDK default change — but we need a runtime-side emergency config to stop immediate deal impact.

- Karthik

Subject: Re: SDK grace-period + rate-limit spike during ingest — runtime analysis and mitigation

Thanks for the repro and logs, Karthik. Quick summary from runtime:
- Root cause: the routing service’s grace-window heuristic currently increases in-flight allowance for routes that transiently hit capacity by holding token reservations open for up to 5s. This was intended to reduce tail errors during short blips but it interacts poorly with aligned client retries. The result is a short period where many requests are allowed through, then the system applies global rate checks and returns 429s in a compressed window.

Proposed immediate action (server-side):
- Push a targeted config change for Atlas’s customer-namespace: set grace-window=500ms and enable smoothing at the edge. This is a runtime config change (no code build) and should take <30 minutes to roll to the customer’s control-plane region after approval.

Longer-term engineering work:
- Implement token-bucket smoothing at the ingress layer and add a per-namespace smoothing weight.
- Add telemetry to detect aligned-retry patterns (histogram of inter-retry arrival times) and raise automated mitigation alerts.

I’ve prepared a small patch diff for the config (attached) and a short rollback plan. If we get sign-off I’ll schedule the emergency config roll and monitor.

Attachment: patch-diff-grace-window-500ms.txt

- Dev

Two asks from Product/GT:

This will be useful for customers who prefer predictable 429s over transient smoothing.
- Karthik, please draft an RFC for the SDK change (jitter default + reduce maxInflight) and include a compatibility migration note.

I’ll notify Ben once the change is live and monitor with Dev.
